# Screen-reader checklist

A manual pass for every component, run before each release. Automated tests already check roles,
names and states (Playwright ARIA snapshots), keyboard scripts, live-region announcements and
axe-core WCAG 2.2 AA in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit. What they cannot check is how a real screen
reader speaks and navigates, so a person does this pass.

**Setup.** Run the docs (`pnpm docs`) and open each component's page; its live examples are the
test surface. Use at least one desktop and one mobile pairing per release, rotating the rest:

| Screen reader | Browser | Platform |
|---|---|---|
| NVDA | Firefox or Chrome | Windows |
| JAWS | Chrome | Windows |
| VoiceOver | Safari | macOS |
| VoiceOver | Safari | iOS |
| TalkBack | Chrome | Android |

**For every component:**
- Tab to it and listen: its role, name, value and state are spoken, and nothing is read twice.
- Use the browse or virtual cursor (NVDA browse mode, VoiceOver VO+arrows) as well as Tab.
- Press each key in its keyboard table and listen for the change to be announced.
- Check each accessibility note below by ear.

**Record** pass or fail per row, with the screen reader, browser and what was spoken. File failures
against the component with that transcript.

**Every page:**
- [ ] Headings and landmarks are listed correctly in the screen reader's rotor or elements list.
- [ ] 200% zoom and 200% text-only zoom: nothing is clipped or overlapping.
- [ ] Windows High Contrast (forced colors): focus and borders stay visible.
- [ ] Reduced motion: nothing animates.
- [ ] Safari: the two-tone focus ring is visible (Playwright's WebKit cannot verify it).


## Actions

### Button (`<focsd-button>`)

Pattern: Button.

- [ ] Native parity: `popovertarget`/`popovertargetaction`, `commandfor`/`command` (built-in dialog and popover commands, or a custom `--name` fired on the target as a `focsd-command` event) and the submit overrides `formaction`, `formmethod`, `formenctype`, `formnovalidate` and `formtarget`. Targets are found by id in the same tree.
- [ ] With submit overrides, the button submits through a temporary native submitter that is removed once the `submit` event has run: read `new FormData(form, event.submitter)` inside the handler, before any `await`.
- [ ] Renders a native `<button>` in its shadow root and delegates focus to it, so it is announced as a button with its slotted text as the name.
- [ ] `disabled` uses `aria-disabled`: the button stays focusable so people can discover it, and activation is swallowed. Explain why nearby, or with a tooltip.
- [ ] `type="submit"` and `type="reset"` act on the owning form, like a native button.
- [ ] Name the outcome ("Save changes", "Remove Lukas"), never "OK" or "Submit".
- [ ] **Enter / Space:** Activates the button

### Link (`<focsd-link>`)

Pattern: Link.

- [ ] `target="_blank"` adds `noopener` and announces "opens in new tab". `download`, `hreflang`, `type`, `referrerpolicy` and `ping` are forwarded.
- [ ] A native `<a>` inside the shadow root, with focus delegated to it.
- [ ] `external` opens a new tab and adds "(opens in new tab)" to the accessible name, so the change of context is announced.
- [ ] **Enter:** Follows the link

### Toggle (`<focsd-toggle>`)

Pattern: Toggle button (aria-pressed).

- [ ] A `<button aria-pressed>`; the label stays the same while the pressed state changes.
- [ ] Use a switch instead when the control changes a setting immediately and persistently.
- [ ] **Enter / Space:** Toggles pressed

### Toggle group (`<focsd-toggle-group>`)

Pattern: Toolbar / radio-like group.

- [ ] A labeled `role="group"` with one tab stop; arrow keys move between toggles (mirrored in right-to-left pages).
- [ ] `type="single"` allows at most one pressed toggle; `type="multiple"` allows any number.
- [ ] Form-associated: submits the pressed value(s) under `name`.
- [ ] **Arrow keys:** Move between toggles
- [ ] **Home / End:** First / last toggle
- [ ] **Enter / Space:** Press the focused toggle

### Icon button (`<focsd-icon-button>`)

Pattern: Button with accessible label.

- [ ] `popovertarget` and `commandfor`/`command` work as on `focsd-button`.
- [ ] Named by `label` through `aria-label`; the icon is decorative (`aria-hidden`).
- [ ] Square at the control height (36px by default), above the 24px target minimum.
- [ ] Pair with a tooltip if sighted users may not recognize the icon.
- [ ] **Enter / Space:** Activates the button

### Button group (`<focsd-button-group>`)

Pattern: Group.

- [ ] A `role="group"` with `aria-label`; each button stays its own tab stop.
- [ ] For a single tab stop with arrow keys, use a toolbar instead.

### Toolbar (`<focsd-toolbar>`)

Pattern: Toolbar.

- [ ] `role="toolbar"` with `aria-label` and `aria-orientation`.
- [ ] Roving tabindex: the toolbar is a single tab stop and arrow keys move between its controls.
- [ ] **Arrow keys:** Move between controls (by orientation)
- [ ] **Home / End:** First / last control

### Split button (`<focsd-split-button>`)

Pattern: Group: button + menu button (Menu Button).

- [ ] Both buttons sit in a group named by `label`. The main button reads the label; the menu button is named "More actions for {label}" ("More actions" when there is no label) and has `aria-haspopup="menu"` and `aria-expanded`.
- [ ] The menu is a `role=menu` of `focsd-menu-item` children with the same keyboard as `focsd-menu`. Disabled items are skipped by the arrow keys and cannot be chosen.
- [ ] Escape, or choosing an item, closes the menu and returns focus to the menu button.
- [ ] The host `click` event comes only from the main button; clicks on the menu button and in the menu stop inside the element. Choosing an item fires `focsd-select` (`detail.value`, `detail.item`).
- [ ] `disabled` turns off both buttons.
- [ ] **Enter / Space / Down:** On the menu button: open the menu on the first item
- [ ] **Up:** On the menu button: open the menu on the last item
- [ ] **Down / Up:** Move between items
- [ ] **Enter / Space:** Choose the focused item
- [ ] **Escape:** Close the menu and return to the menu button

### Copy button (`<focsd-copy-button>`)

Pattern: Button + polite status.

- [ ] The button is named "Copy" unless you set `label`; name it after what it copies when a page has several ("Copy API key").
- [ ] The name stays the same after a copy. A polite status region says "Copied" (or `copied-label`), and the icon turns to a check for 2 seconds (an alert icon when the copy failed).
- [ ] When the browser refuses the write, the status says "Copy failed" and the element fires `focsd-error`; it never says "Copied" for a copy that did not happen.
- [ ] With `from`, it copies the value of the form control with that id, or the trimmed text of any other element. Without the Clipboard API (pages not served over HTTPS) it falls back to `execCommand('copy')`.
- [ ] It fires `focsd-copy` with `detail.text` after a copy. `focsd-code` uses it for its "Copy code" button.
- [ ] **Enter / Space:** Copy the text

### Dock (`<focsd-dock>`)

Pattern: Radio group (selection follows focus).

- [ ] A radio group named by `label` (default "Views"), with each item a radio named by its text. Screen readers say "Search, radio button, 2 of 4".
- [ ] Each label shows as a tip on hover and on keyboard focus (Escape hides it), so sighted people can learn what an icon means. Set `label-display="shown"` to show the labels under the icons instead.
- [ ] The dock is an opaque raised surface with an edge and a shadow, so its icons stay readable over any content behind it. `--focsd-dock-background`, `--focsd-dock-border-color`, `--focsd-dock-shadow` and `--focsd-dock-radius` restyle it.
- [ ] Selection follows focus: one arrow press moves and chooses. Use it when the choice shows at once, such as a filter or a view.
- [ ] The selected item has a filled surface, full-strength text and a bar under it, so color is never the only cue. In forced colors it takes the system selected-item colors.
- [ ] Every item is as tall as the density's controls (32, 36 or 44 px), so the dock lines up with buttons and fields beside it, and never under the 24 px target size.
- [ ] Not for links between pages: use `focsd-bottom-nav` or `focsd-nav-menu`, which are real links in a navigation landmark.
- [ ] **Arrow keys:** Move to the next or previous item and select it (Left and Right swap in right-to-left text)
- [ ] **Home / End:** First / last item
- [ ] **Tab:** Move into the dock, then out of it

Labels under the icons, your own icons and sizes:

- [ ] The icon is decoration and hidden from assistive technology; the label always names the item, shown or not.
- [ ] Show the labels when the icons are not ones everyone knows: visible labels are easier for everyone, and on touch screens there is no hover.

## Forms

### Text field (`<focsd-text-field>`)

Pattern: Native input.

- [ ] Native parity: `minlength`, `maxlength`, `pattern`, `size`, `inputmode`, `enterkeyhint`, `autocapitalize`, `autocorrect`, `spellcheck`, `dirname`, `readonly`, `setCustomValidity()` and the selection APIs (`select()`, `setSelectionRange()`, `setRangeText()`). Give personal-data fields an `autocomplete` token (WCAG 1.3.5). Not supported: `list` (datalist), because the ID reference cannot cross into shadow DOM. Use `focsd-combobox`.
- [ ] The label, hint and error render in the same shadow root as the `<input>`, so `for` and `aria-describedby` always resolve.
- [ ] An `error` sets `aria-invalid` and is read with the field; native constraint failures are announced after a failed submit.
- [ ] Hints and messages are part of the description; a new message is announced politely.
- [ ] Only one of `error`, `warning` and `success` shows, in that order. `warning` and `success` never block submission.
- [ ] Built-in validation: `error-message` is the text shown when the field fails `required`, `type`, `pattern`, `min` and the like (on submit, or `validate()`); it clears once the value is fixed. `warning-pattern` with `warning-message` shows a non-blocking warning while the value does not match. Inside a form with `focsd-error-summary`, no script is needed.
- [ ] Never use the placeholder as the label.
- [ ] Form-associated: participates in `FormData`, validation, reset and fieldset `disabled` like a native control.
- [ ] **Enter:** Submits the owning form

### Select (`<focsd-select>`)

Pattern: Listbox button (popover).

- [ ] Do not set `readonly` here: like a native checkbox or select it has no effect, and HTML skips validation for any custom form control with a `readonly` attribute. Use `disabled`, or show the value as text.
- [ ] `multiple` makes an `aria-multiselectable` listbox that stays open while options are toggled; the form receives one entry per value. `selectedIndex`, `selectedOptions`, `length`, `showPicker()` and option `selected`, `defaultSelected`, `label`, `index` and `text` work as on native elements. Not supported: `size` (use `focsd-list selectable` for an always-open list) and `autocomplete` (browsers only autofill native controls; use `focsd-combobox` or a native `<select>` for personal-data fields, WCAG 1.3.5).
- [ ] A button with `aria-haspopup="listbox"` opens a `role="listbox"` popover; focus moves into it and returns to the button on close.
- [ ] Typeahead jumps to matching options; disabled options (and options in a disabled group) are skipped.
- [ ] `focsd-option-group` makes a named `role="group"` inside the listbox, like `<optgroup>`; its `disabled` disables every option in it.
- [ ] `searchable` adds a filter box (a named searchbox) above the list; groups with no match are hidden. `select-all` adds a Select all / Deselect all button, and `max` stops further choices once reached (announced in a status).
- [ ] `clearable` adds a "Clear <label>" button that empties the selection and returns focus to the select.
- [ ] Form-associated: participates in `FormData`, validation, reset and fieldset `disabled` like a native control.
- [ ] **Enter / Space / Arrow Down / Arrow Up:** Open the list at the selected option
- [ ] **Home / End (closed):** Open the list at the first / last option
- [ ] **Arrow Up / Down:** Move through options
- [ ] **Home / End (open):** First / last option
- [ ] **Enter / Space:** Choose the option and close
- [ ] **Escape:** Close without changing
- [ ] **Tab:** Close and move on
- [ ] **Type a letter (open list):** Jump to a matching option
- [ ] **Enter / Space (multiple):** Toggle the option; the list stays open
- [ ] **Arrow Down (filter box):** Move to the first matching option
- [ ] **Arrow Up (first option):** Back to the filter box

### Textarea (`<focsd-textarea>`)

Pattern: Native textarea.

- [ ] `cols`, `wrap` and `textLength` work as on a native textarea.
- [ ] With `maxlength`, a polite live counter ("12 of 120 characters") is announced as people type.
- [ ] Form-associated: participates in `FormData`, validation, reset and fieldset `disabled` like a native control.

### Checkbox (`<focsd-checkbox>`)

Pattern: Checkbox (incl. mixed).

- [ ] Do not set `readonly` here: like a native checkbox or select it has no effect, and HTML skips validation for any custom form control with a `readonly` attribute. Use `disabled`, or show the value as text.
- [ ] A native checkbox inside a `<label>` that wraps the slotted text, so clicking the text toggles it.
- [ ] `indeterminate` exposes the mixed state.
- [ ] `required` reports `valueMissing` until checked.
- [ ] Form-associated: participates in `FormData`, validation, reset and fieldset `disabled` like a native control.
- [ ] **Space:** Toggles

### Checkbox group (`<focsd-checkbox-group>`)

Pattern: Group + fieldset.

- [ ] A shadow `<fieldset>` and `<legend>` give the checkboxes a group name; the hint and error render inside it.
- [ ] Each checkbox submits on its own.

### Radio group (`<focsd-radio-group>`)

Pattern: Radio group.

- [ ] Do not set `readonly` here: like a native checkbox or select it has no effect, and HTML skips validation for any custom form control with a `readonly` attribute. Use `disabled`, or show the value as text.
- [ ] `role="radiogroup"` labeled by its legend; each `focsd-radio` host is `role="radio"` with `aria-checked`.
- [ ] One tab stop. Arrow keys move and check, skipping disabled radios.
- [ ] Form-associated: participates in `FormData`, validation, reset and fieldset `disabled` like a native control.
- [ ] **Arrow keys:** Move to and check the next/previous radio
- [ ] **Space:** Check the focused radio

### Switch (`<focsd-switch>`)

Pattern: Switch.

- [ ] Do not set `readonly` here: like a native checkbox or select it has no effect, and HTML skips validation for any custom form control with a `readonly` attribute. Use `disabled`, or show the value as text.
- [ ] A `<button role="switch" aria-checked>` labeled by the slotted text.
- [ ] Shows visible On/Off text, so the state never relies on color or position alone.
- [ ] Form-associated: participates in `FormData`, validation, reset and fieldset `disabled` like a native control.
- [ ] **Space / Enter:** Toggles

### Number field (`<focsd-number-field>`)

Pattern: Spinbutton.

- [ ] `valueAsNumber`, `stepUp()` and `stepDown()` work as on a native number input.
- [ ] `role="spinbutton"` with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin` and `aria-valuemax`.
- [ ] The +/− buttons are named "Increase Seats" / "Decrease Seats" and kept out of the tab order; the keyboard does the same job.
- [ ] Form-associated: participates in `FormData`, validation, reset and fieldset `disabled` like a native control.
- [ ] **Arrow Up / Down:** Step by `step`
- [ ] **Page Up / Down:** Step by 10 × `step`
- [ ] **Home / End:** Jump to min / max (when set)

### Search field (`<focsd-search-field>`)

Pattern: Searchbox.

- [ ] A native `type="search"` input (role searchbox).
- [ ] The "Clear search" button appears when there is a value.
- [ ] Form-associated: participates in `FormData`, validation, reset and fieldset `disabled` like a native control.
- [ ] **Escape:** Clears the value

### Password field (`<focsd-password-field>`)

Pattern: Input + visibility toggle.

- [ ] The "Show password" toggle is a `<button aria-pressed>`; its name stays constant while the pressed state changes.
- [ ] Toggling keeps focus and the caret position.
- [ ] `autocomplete` defaults to `current-password`; use `new-password` on sign-up forms.
- [ ] Form-associated: participates in `FormData`, validation, reset and fieldset `disabled` like a native control.

### Slider (`<focsd-slider>`)

Pattern: Slider (single + range).

- [ ] Do not set `readonly` here: like a native checkbox or select it has no effect, and HTML skips validation for any custom form control with a `readonly` attribute. Use `disabled`, or show the value as text.
- [ ] `valueAsNumber`, `stepUp()` and `stepDown()` work as on a native range input.
- [ ] Each thumb is `role="slider"` with `aria-valuenow/min/max` and `aria-valuetext` from the `value-text` template.
- [ ] Range thumbs are named "Minimum Price" and "Maximum Price" and cannot cross.
- [ ] Form-associated: participates in `FormData`, validation, reset and fieldset `disabled` like a native control.
- [ ] **Arrow keys:** Step by `step`
- [ ] **Page Up / Down:** Step by 10 × `step`
- [ ] **Home / End:** Jump to min / max

### OTP input (`<focsd-otp-field>`)

Pattern: Grouped inputs.

- [ ] `autocomplete` defaults to `one-time-code`, so browsers can fill codes from SMS.
- [ ] A labeled `role="group"`; each cell is named "Digit n of 6".
- [ ] Pasting a code fills the cells from the first one.
- [ ] The cells take the field's state: `error`, `warning` and `success` (or `error-message` and `warning-pattern` with `warning-message`, checked for you) color every cell's border and show the message under the group.
- [ ] Form-associated: participates in `FormData`, validation, reset and fieldset `disabled` like a native control.
- [ ] **Digits:** Fill the cell and move to the next
- [ ] **Backspace (empty cell):** Clear the previous cell and move to it
- [ ] **Arrow Left / Right:** Previous / next cell

### Fieldset (`<focsd-fieldset>`)

Pattern: Fieldset + legend.

- [ ] `disabled` disables every control inside (native or Focsd), leaving them out of validation and the form data, like a native fieldset. Controls you disabled yourself stay disabled when the fieldset is enabled again.
- [ ] A shadow `<fieldset>` with `<legend>`; screen readers announce the legend when focus enters the group.

### Error summary (`<focsd-error-summary>`)

Pattern: Alert with links to fields.

- [ ] `role="alert"` and `tabindex="-1"`: it takes focus on a submit with errors, so the problem is announced. It does not move focus while a fix shortens the list.
- [ ] Each error is a link that moves focus to its field (works with shadow-DOM fields).
- [ ] Each field shows its own error too (a 1px critical border, an icon and the message), so the error never relies on color or on the summary alone.

### Rating (`<focsd-rating>`)

Pattern: Radio group.

- [ ] Interactive: a `role="radiogroup"` of star radios named "1 star", "2 stars"…, one tab stop.
- [ ] Read-only: `role="img"` named by the label and value ("Average rating: 4 out of 5").
- [ ] Form-associated: participates in `FormData`, validation, reset and fieldset `disabled` like a native control.
- [ ] **Arrow keys:** Change the rating (wraps around)
- [ ] **Home / End:** One star / the maximum
- [ ] **Space:** Choose the focused star

### Combobox (`<focsd-combobox>`)

Pattern: Combobox (autocomplete).

- [ ] `autocomplete` is forwarded to the input (for example `country-name`, WCAG 1.3.5).
- [ ] APG combobox with list autocomplete: focus stays in the input and the active option is referenced with `aria-activedescendant`.
- [ ] Slotted `focsd-option`s are data; the visible list is rendered inside the same shadow root as the input, so the reference never crosses a shadow boundary.
- [ ] A polite status announces the result count ("3 results", "No results").
- [ ] `focsd-option-group` children render as named groups in the list; a group hides when none of its options match.
- [ ] `multiple` turns it into a multi-select (the same as `focsd-multi-select`). `clearable` adds a "Clear <label>" button.
- [ ] Typed text that does not match an option is discarded on blur; clearing the text clears the value. Set `allow-custom` to accept free text.
- [ ] Form-associated: participates in `FormData`, validation, reset, fieldset `disabled` and back/forward restore.
- [ ] **Arrow Down / Up:** Open and move through options
- [ ] **Alt + Arrow Down:** Open without moving
- [ ] **Enter:** Choose the active option
- [ ] **Escape:** Close; press again to clear

### Multi-select (`<focsd-multi-select>`)

Pattern: Combobox + tags.

- [ ] A combobox with an `aria-multiselectable` listbox; Enter toggles and keeps the list open.
- [ ] Each tag has a "Remove Bug" button.
- [ ] `value` is comma-separated; the form receives one entry per value.
- [ ] Shorthand for `<focsd-combobox multiple>`: groups, `clearable`, `max` and `select-all` work the same. Select all is the first row of the list (focus stays in the input), and it only picks options matching the current filter, up to `max`.
- [ ] Form-associated: participates in `FormData`, validation, reset, fieldset `disabled` and back/forward restore.
- [ ] **Arrow keys:** Move through options
- [ ] **Enter:** Toggle the active option
- [ ] **Backspace (empty input):** Remove the last tag
- [ ] **Escape:** Close the list; press again to clear the typed text

### Calendar (`<focsd-calendar>`)

Pattern: Grid (date).

- [ ] APG date grid: `role="grid"` labeled by the month heading, which is a polite live region.
- [ ] Each day has a full accessible name ("Saturday, 14 March 2026"), `aria-selected`, `aria-current="date"` for today, and `aria-disabled` outside `min`/`max`.
- [ ] One tab stop (roving tabindex); arrows are mirrored in right-to-left pages. The first day of the week comes from the locale.
- [ ] **Arrow keys:** Previous / next day or week
- [ ] **Page Up / Down:** Previous / next month
- [ ] **Shift + Page Up / Down:** Previous / next year
- [ ] **Home / End:** Start / end of the week
- [ ] **Enter / Space:** Select the day

Events and a legend:

- [ ] The dots are decorative: each day's accessible name includes its events and their kinds ("Tuesday, November 17, 2026, Team sync (Meeting), Design critique (Review)"), and a tooltip shows them on hover, so nothing depends on color.
- [ ] The legend is a list labeled "Event types" (localizable as `calendarLegend`).
- [ ] Up to three dots show per day; every event is still named in the label.

### Date picker (`<focsd-date-picker>`)

Pattern: Dialog + grid.

- [ ] `autocomplete`, `step` (in days), `valueAsDate`, `valueAsNumber` and `showPicker()` work as on a native date input.
- [ ] Typing is always allowed: the input shows the expected format ("YYYY-MM-DD") in its description and reports invalid or out-of-range dates.
- [ ] The "Choose date" button opens a modal `<dialog>` labeled "Choose date"; focus lands on the selected day and returns to the button on close.
- [ ] Form-associated: participates in `FormData`, validation, reset, fieldset `disabled` and back/forward restore.
- [ ] **Enter (in the input):** Submit the form
- [ ] **Calendar keys:** As the calendar
- [ ] **Escape:** Close the dialog without changing

### Date range picker (`<focsd-date-range-picker>`)

Pattern: Dialog + grid.

- [ ] `autocomplete` is forwarded to both inputs.
- [ ] A `role="group"` named by the label, with two labeled inputs ("Start date", "End date") and one "Choose dates" button.
- [ ] In the dialog the first pick sets the start and the second the end; every day in the range is `aria-selected`.
- [ ] The form receives `<name>-start` and `<name>-end`.
- [ ] Form-associated: participates in `FormData`, validation, reset, fieldset `disabled` and back/forward restore.

### Time field (`<focsd-time-field>`)

Pattern: Spinbutton segments.

- [ ] `min`, `max`, `valueAsDate`, `valueAsNumber`, `stepUp()` and `stepDown()` work as on a native time input; `step` is in minutes. Not supported: `autocomplete` (the segments are not native inputs). Use a native `<input type="time">` where autofill matters.
- [ ] A labeled `role="group"` of `role="spinbutton"` segments named "Hours", "Minutes" (and "AM/PM" in 12-hour mode), each with `aria-valuetext`.
- [ ] Segments stay in hours-then-minutes order in every script direction.
- [ ] The form value is always 24-hour `HH:MM`.
- [ ] Form-associated: participates in `FormData`, validation, reset, fieldset `disabled` and back/forward restore.
- [ ] **Arrow Up / Down:** Change the segment
- [ ] **Digits:** Type a value; moves on when complete
- [ ] **Arrow Left / Right:** Previous / next segment
- [ ] **A / P (AM/PM segment):** Set AM / PM
- [ ] **Backspace / Delete:** Clear the segment

### File upload (`<focsd-file-upload>`)

Pattern: Button + drop zone + list.

- [ ] `capture`, `webkitdirectory` and `showPicker()` reach the native file picker.
- [ ] A visible "Choose files" button opens the native picker, so dragging is never required (WCAG 2.5.7).
- [ ] Rejected files are reported in a `role="alert"` region and never added; a polite status reports "2 files selected".
- [ ] Each file has a "Remove report.pdf" button; focus returns to the choose button after removal.
- [ ] Files cannot be restored after back/forward navigation (browsers do not allow it).

### Rich text editor (`<focsd-rich-text>`)

Pattern: Textbox (multi-line, contenteditable) + toolbar.

- [ ] A multi-line `role="textbox"` named by its label, with the hint or error as its description.
- [ ] The toolbar is an APG toolbar: one tab stop, arrow keys between buttons, `aria-pressed` for formats, and `aria-keyshortcuts` for each shortcut.
- [ ] The value is HTML limited to the toolbar's formats: scripts, event handlers and unsafe links are removed, and links only accept web, mail, phone or same-site addresses.
- [ ] Form-associated: `name`, `required`, `disabled`, `readonly`, reset and `setCustomValidity` work like a textarea.
- [ ] Separate package (`@focsd-dev/editor`, about 141 KB gzip with Tiptap and ProseMirror): load it only on pages that need it, for example with `import('@focsd-dev/editor')`.
- [ ] **Ctrl/Cmd + B, I, U:** Bold, italic, underline
- [ ] **Ctrl/Cmd + K:** Add or edit a link
- [ ] **Ctrl/Cmd + Alt + 2 / 3:** Heading 2 / 3
- [ ] **Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + 7 / 8:** Numbered / bulleted list
- [ ] **Ctrl/Cmd + Z, Shift + Z:** Undo, redo
- [ ] **Tab / Shift + Tab (in a list):** Indent / outdent the item; elsewhere Tab leaves the editor
- [ ] **Arrow keys (toolbar):** Move between buttons

### Color picker (`<focsd-color-picker>`)

Pattern: 2D slider + sliders + text field + swatches.

- [ ] The saturation and brightness area is one `role="slider"` whose `aria-valuetext` reads both values ("Saturation 80%, brightness 40%").
- [ ] Every part works by keyboard, and the text field accepts any CSS color, so dragging is never required (WCAG 2.5.7).
- [ ] Swatches are a `role="radiogroup"` with roving focus; each swatch is named by its color or label.
- [ ] With `contrast-with`, a polite status reports the WCAG contrast ratio against that color.
- [ ] The pick-from-screen button only appears where the browser supports the EyeDropper API.
- [ ] **Left / Right:** Saturation (area), hue or opacity (sliders)
- [ ] **Up / Down:** Brightness (area), hue or opacity (sliders)
- [ ] **Shift + arrows:** Bigger steps
- [ ] **Page Up / Down:** Brightness ±10 (area), hue ±30° or opacity ±10% (sliders)
- [ ] **Home / End:** Saturation 0 / 100 (area), minimum / maximum (sliders)
- [ ] **Arrow keys (swatches):** Move between swatches; Enter or Space picks one
- [ ] **Enter:** Apply the typed color
- [ ] **Escape:** Close the popover and return to the button

### Tag input (`<focsd-tag-input>`)

Pattern: Text input + list of removable tags (+ optional listbox).

- [ ] Tags are a list; each has a "Remove {tag}" button.
- [ ] Adding, removing, duplicates and the maximum are announced in a polite status.
- [ ] Pasting a list (commas or new lines) adds every item at once.
- [ ] With `focsd-option` suggestions the input is an APG combobox with `aria-activedescendant`.
- [ ] The form gets one entry per tag under `name`, so servers never split a string.
- [ ] **Enter, comma (the `separator`) or Tab:** Add the typed text as a tag
- [ ] **Shift+Tab (in the input):** Move to the tags: the one last visited, or the last tag
- [ ] **Tab / Shift+Tab (on a tag):** Move to the input / leave the component: the tags are one tab stop
- [ ] **Backspace (empty input):** Move to the last tag
- [ ] **Backspace / Delete on a tag:** Remove it
- [ ] **Left / Right:** Move between tags and the input
- [ ] **Home / End (on a tag):** First tag / back to the input
- [ ] **Down / Up:** Move through suggestions
- [ ] **Escape:** Close the suggestions

Sortable:

- [ ] With `sortable`, each tag gets a "Reorder {tag}" button before its text. It shares the one tab stop of the remove buttons; the arrow keys move between all tag buttons.
- [ ] Grabbing, each move, the drop and a cancel are announced in the tag input’s polite status.
- [ ] A drop updates `values` (the form gets the tags in the new order) and fires `input` and `change`, after a cancelable `focsd-reorder` with `detail.from`, `detail.to` and `detail.value`.
- [ ] **Space / Enter (on a handle):** Grab the tag, or drop it
- [ ] **Arrow keys:** Move the grabbed tag one place (Left and Right mirrored right to left)
- [ ] **Escape:** Put the tag back where it was

### Phone field (`<focsd-phone-field>`)

Pattern: Group: country combobox + tel input, E.164 value.

- [ ] One `role="group"` named by the label holds a "Country" combobox and a `type="tel"` input.
- [ ] The tel input is described by your `hint`, then an example number for the chosen country, then the shown message, and uses `autocomplete="tel-national"`. Style the example with `::part(example)`; `::part(hint)` is your hint, as on every control.
- [ ] Typing or pasting a number with `+` or `00` switches the country, announced in a polite status.
- [ ] Invalid numbers report "Enter a valid United Kingdom phone number"; pass `validator` for stricter checks.
- [ ] The value and the form entry are E.164 (`+442071838750`), so servers never parse local formats.
- [ ] **Type in Country:** Filter by name, code or dial code (+353)
- [ ] **Down / Up:** Move through countries
- [ ] **Home / End (open list):** First / last country
- [ ] **Enter:** Choose the country
- [ ] **Escape:** Close the list and keep the country

### Currency field (`<focsd-currency-field>`)

Pattern: Spinbutton with locale-formatted currency.

- [ ] An APG `role="spinbutton"` whose `aria-valuetext` is the formatted amount ("€1,234.50").
- [ ] The currency name and code are part of the accessible description.
- [ ] Typing accepts the page language's decimal and group symbols and pasted currency signs.
- [ ] The value and form entry are a dot-decimal string with the currency's decimals ("1234.50", "100" for yen).
- [ ] Out-of-range amounts report a formatted message ("Enter €10,000.00 or less").
- [ ] **Arrow Up / Down:** Step by `step` (default: the smallest unit, such as one cent)
- [ ] **Page Up / Down:** Step by 10 × `step`
- [ ] **Home / End:** Jump to min / max (when set)
- [ ] **Enter:** Submits the owning form

### Field (`<focsd-field>`)

Pattern: Label, hint and messages for any control (light-DOM IDs).

- [ ] The label is a real `<label for>` for labelable controls (native inputs and form-associated elements); for any other `[slot="control"]` element it sets `aria-labelledby`.
- [ ] The hint and message are light-DOM siblings of the control, referenced by `aria-describedby` (shadow roots cannot share IDs). The field keeps any `aria-describedby` ids you set.
- [ ] `error` uses `setCustomValidity` where the control has it, so it blocks submission, and sets `aria-invalid`; clearing it undoes both. `warning` and `success` never block.
- [ ] A message that changes after the first render is announced politely; one present at first render is only described.
- [ ] The required marker is hidden from assistive technology: set `required` on the control itself so the name and state are read.
- [ ] One control per field: only the first is labeled and described, so use one field per control.
- [ ] The field has no role of its own. Author content is never replaced; generated nodes carry `data-focsd-field`.

### Date field (`<focsd-date-field>`)

Pattern: Spinbutton segments (day, month, year).

- [ ] A labeled `role="group"` of `role="spinbutton"` segments named "Day", "Month" and "Year", in the order the locale writes them. The month segment speaks its name ("March") through `aria-valuetext`; an empty segment reads "Empty".
- [ ] Impossible dates, such as February 30 or February 29 in a year that is not a leap year, are never moved to a nearby day: `value` stays empty and the field reports "Enter a real date, such as 2026-02-28."
- [ ] A year only counts once all four digits are typed. Leaving a segment halfway through clears it, so "19" is never read as the year 19.
- [ ] Pasting `2026-10-15`, or a date written in the locale order such as `15/10/2026` in `en-GB`, fills every segment. Only digits count: a two-digit year, or a date with a month name such as "Oct 15, 2026", is ignored.
- [ ] `min`, `max`, `required` and `valueAsDate` work as on a native date input, with plain messages for each. The form value is always `YYYY-MM-DD`.
- [ ] Form-associated: participates in `FormData`, validation, reset, fieldset `disabled` and back/forward restore. Restore brings back a half-typed date.
- [ ] **Arrow Up / Down:** Change the segment; wraps at the ends
- [ ] **Digits:** Type a value; moves on when complete
- [ ] **Arrow Left / Right:** Previous / next segment
- [ ] **Backspace / Delete:** Clear the segment; Backspace on an empty segment moves to the previous one
- [ ] **Paste:** Fill every segment from an ISO or locale date

### Listbox (`<focsd-listbox>`)

Pattern: Listbox (aria-activedescendant).

- [ ] A labeled `role="listbox"` that takes focus itself; the active option is pointed to with `aria-activedescendant`, so screen readers read each option as the arrows move. Groups are named `role="group"`s.
- [ ] With one value, the selection follows the active option, as in a native list box. With `multiple`, the list is `aria-multiselectable` and moving never changes the selection on its own: Space does.
- [ ] Disabled options are announced as unavailable and skipped by the arrows and by typing. The arrows stop at the first and last option instead of wrapping.
- [ ] Listbox or list? Use `focsd-listbox` for a form value that should always be on screen: it is form-associated and submits one entry per selected value. Use `focsd-list` with `selectable` for navigation-style choice, such as picking which message to read.
- [ ] Options are data: each row shows the option's `label` (or its text), not rich content such as icons or markup inside the `focsd-option`. Set the selection with the listbox's `value` or `values`; writing `option.selected` from code does not change it (the `selected` attribute sets the default). Give each option its `value` as an attribute: a `value` set only as a property on a `focsd-option` is not picked up until the options change again.
- [ ] Form-associated: participates in `FormData`, `required` validation, reset (back to the `value` attribute or the options marked `selected`), fieldset `disabled` and back/forward restore.
- [ ] **Arrow Down / Up:** Next / previous option (Right / Left with `orientation="horizontal"`)
- [ ] **Home / End:** First / last option
- [ ] **Letters:** Next option starting with the letters typed; type quickly to search several
- [ ] **Space:** Select or clear the active option (`multiple`)
- [ ] **Shift + Arrow:** Select from the last chosen option to the next one; moving back deselects (`multiple`)
- [ ] **Shift + Space:** Select every option from the last chosen one to the active one (`multiple`)
- [ ] **Ctrl / ⌘ + A:** Select every option, or none when all are selected (`multiple`)

### Date and time picker (`<focsd-date-time-picker>`)

Pattern: Group: date input + dialog (calendar, time) + time field.

- [ ] One labeled `role="group"` holds a text input named "Date", a "Choose date and time" button and a time field named "Time", so each part can be typed without opening the dialog.
- [ ] The button opens a modal dialog named "Choose date and time" with the calendar, a second time field and a Done button. Picking a day keeps the dialog open; Done applies the day and time, closes it and returns focus to the button. Escape closes it and changes nothing.
- [ ] There is no time zone. The value is the local wall-clock time, `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm`, as on a native `datetime-local` input; your app converts it to or from a zone or UTC.
- [ ] `min` and `max` use the same format and compare the whole timestamp, so `2026-03-01T07:45` is before a `min` of `2026-03-01T08:00`. `step` is in minutes and sets how far the arrow keys move the minutes. Values have minute precision: seconds in `value`, `min` or `max` (`09:30:59`) are accepted and dropped.
- [ ] A date without a time, or a time without a date, reports "Enter a date and time." `required` reports the same message when both are empty.
- [ ] Form-associated: participates in `FormData`, validation, reset, fieldset `disabled` and back/forward restore.
- [ ] **Tab:** Date input, then the dialog button, then the time segments
- [ ] **Arrow keys (calendar):** Move between days; Enter picks one and keeps the dialog open
- [ ] **Arrow Up / Down (time):** Change hours or minutes by `step`
- [ ] **Digits (time):** Type hours and minutes; moves on when complete
- [ ] **Escape:** Close the dialog without changing the value

### Swatch picker (`<focsd-swatch-picker>`)

Pattern: Radio group of swatches + custom color popover.

- [ ] A `role="radiogroup"` named by the label. The `color` attribute of an option is its color (its `value` is used only when there is no `color`), and the value that is set and submitted is that color as lower-case hex. Each swatch is a radio named by its option text, else the CSS color name that matches exactly (such as "tomato"), else its hex value. Color names are English; give options a `label` to localize them.
- [ ] The chosen swatch shows a check mark and a ring, so the choice is not shown by color alone. Swatch borders keep 3:1 against the surface, and swatches keep their colors in forced-colors mode.
- [ ] One tab stop. Arrow keys move to the next swatch and choose it, and wrap at the ends; skipped swatches are disabled ones.
- [ ] With `allow-custom`, a "Custom color" button opens a popup with a color picker. Escape closes it and returns focus to the button. A custom color shows a check mark on the button; no radio is checked.
- [ ] Form-associated: submits the lower-case hex value, supports `required`, reset, fieldset `disabled` and restore. A restored value that is not a color, or not a swatch without `allow-custom`, becomes empty.
- [ ] **Tab:** Moves to the chosen swatch (or the first), then to the custom color button
- [ ] **Arrow keys:** Move to the next or previous swatch and choose it
- [ ] **Home / End:** First or last swatch
- [ ] **Space / Enter:** Choose the focused swatch, or open the custom color popup
- [ ] **Escape:** Close the custom color popup

### Editable (`<focsd-editable>`)

Pattern: Button that switches to a text field.

- [ ] Display mode is a button named "label: value, edit" (the visible label comes first, so the name starts with it). With no value it reads the placeholder, or "Empty".
- [ ] Editing swaps in a text field (a textarea with `multiline`) named by the label. The text is selected and focused. A commit refused because the value is blank with `required`, or invalid, keeps the editor open and shows the error as its description.
- [ ] Focus returns to the button after Enter or Escape. Moving focus to another element commits unless `keep-open-on-blur` is set, which keeps the draft open. Switching windows or tabs neither commits nor cancels.
- [ ] Escape stops there, so a dialog around the editable stays open. Enter during IME composition picks a candidate and does not commit.
- [ ] Fires one `input` and one `change` for a commit that changed the value, and nothing while typing. Escape fires `focsd-cancel`. Reset and restore leave edit mode without events.
- [ ] **Enter / Space:** On the button: start editing
- [ ] **Enter:** In a single line: commit
- [ ] **Ctrl/Cmd + Enter:** In multiline: commit (Enter adds a new line)
- [ ] **Escape:** Cancel and restore the previous value

### Segmented control (`<focsd-segmented-control>`)

Pattern: Radio group (selection follows focus).

- [ ] A radio group: the control is named by its `label` and each segment is a radio. Screen readers say "Week, radio button, 2 of 4, selected".
- [ ] Selection follows focus, so one arrow press both moves and chooses. Use it when the choice takes effect at once, and a radio group when the person confirms with a button.
- [ ] One tab stop for the whole row. Disabled segments are skipped; the arrows wrap from the last segment to the first.
- [ ] Every segment is at least 44 px tall at every `size`, and under 20rem wide the segments stack so the labels never shrink.
- [ ] It is form-associated: `name`, `value`, `required`, `disabled`, `hint` and messages work as on `focsd-radio-group`, and a form reset restores the value it started with.
- [ ] Not a toolbar: for several buttons that each switch on and off, use `focsd-toggle-group`. [Choosing a toggle](/guides/choosing-a-toggle/) compares them.
- [ ] **Arrow keys:** Move to the next or previous segment and select it (Left and Right swap in right-to-left text)
- [ ] **Home / End:** First / last segment
- [ ] **Tab:** Move into the group, then out of it

Sizes and icons:

- [ ] The icon is decoration: the segment is named by its text, so an icon never replaces the label.
- [ ] Size changes the font and the inline padding only. Targets stay 44 px tall.
- [ ] In forced colors the selected segment uses the system selected-item colors, not a tint.

### Signature pad (`<focsd-signature-pad>`)

Pattern: Image (role=img) with a typed-name alternative.

- [ ] Drawing is not the only way in. "Type instead" turns the pad into a text field labeled "Type your name for Signature", and the name is drawn as a typed signature. People who cannot draw, or use a keyboard or a screen reader, sign this way.
- [ ] The group is named by the label and described by the hint and any message (read once when focus enters). The canvas is an image named "Signature, signed" or "Signature, empty". A polite status says "Signature added" or "Signature cleared" after each change. When `required` and empty, the message is "Add your signature."
- [ ] It uses pointer events, so mouse, touch and pen all work, and it keeps `touch-action: none` on the canvas only, so the page still scrolls around it.
- [ ] `required` with an empty pad gives the "Required" message, anchored on the mode button (or on the typed field in typed mode).
- [ ] The form receives a PNG file named `signature.png`, plus `signature-typed` set to `true` when the name was typed. It is empty, not a blank image, until someone signs.
- [ ] The ink is black unless you set `pen-color`, so a signature stays readable on paper in a dark theme. In forced colors the canvas draws in the system text color.
- [ ] Agents never fill this field: WebMCP leaves the signature pad out of its tools, so nothing signs on a person's behalf.
- [ ] **Tab:** Move through Type instead (or Draw instead), Undo and Clear
- [ ] **Enter / Space:** Press the focused button
- [ ] **Type your name:** In typed mode, an ordinary text field

## Overlays

### Dialog (`<focsd-dialog>`)

Pattern: Dialog (modal).

- [ ] `requestClose()` and Escape fire a cancelable `cancel`; `showModal()` is an alias of `show()`. `closedby="any"` also closes on a backdrop click; `closedby="none"` needs an explicit close action.
- [ ] Built on native `<dialog>.showModal()`: top layer, inert background, Escape to close.
- [ ] A close (×) button named "Close" sits in the top corner and asks to close as Escape does (a cancelable `cancel`). It comes last in the tab order, so opening the dialog focuses its content first. Add `no-close` for a dialog that must be answered with one of its actions.
- [ ] Open it from a button with no script: `<focsd-button commandfor="dialog-id" command="show-modal">`. Focus returns to that button on close. From your own code, call `show(opener)`.
- [ ] Any slotted element with `data-dialog-close` closes it; its `value` becomes `returnValue`. Put `data-autofocus` on the element that should receive focus first.
- [ ] **Tab:** Moves focus within the dialog; the page behind is inert
- [ ] **Escape:** Closes (unless `closedby="none"`)

### Popover (`<focsd-popover>`)

Pattern: Non-modal dialog (popover API).

- [ ] The panel is a non-modal `role="dialog"` named by `label`; the trigger gets `aria-expanded` and `aria-haspopup="dialog"`.
- [ ] Focus moves to the first focusable element in the panel and returns to the trigger on Escape or outside click.
- [ ] `closable` adds a close (×) button named "Close" to the panel, useful on touch screens and for panels with a form. It returns focus to the trigger.
- [ ] Positioned with CSS anchor positioning in the top layer (`popover` API).
- [ ] **Enter / Space (trigger):** Open or close
- [ ] **Escape:** Close and return focus to the trigger

### Tooltip (`<focsd-tooltip>`)

Pattern: Tooltip (hover + focus, Esc).

- [ ] The trigger gets the text as `aria-description`, so it is read with the control; the visual tooltip is `aria-hidden` to avoid double reading.
- [ ] Stays open while hovered and dismisses on Escape (WCAG 1.4.13).
- [ ] Never put essential information or interactive content in a tooltip.
- [ ] **Tab (to the trigger):** Show
- [ ] **Escape:** Hide

### Dropdown menu (`<focsd-menu>`)

Pattern: Menu button.

- [ ] APG menu button: the trigger gets `aria-haspopup="menu"` and `aria-expanded`; items are `role="menuitem"`.
- [ ] Choosing an item fires `focsd-select` with `detail.value`, closes the menu and returns focus to the trigger.
- [ ] **Enter / Space / Arrow Down:** Open at the first item
- [ ] **Arrow Up:** Open at the last item
- [ ] **Arrow Up / Down:** Move (wrapping, skips disabled items)
- [ ] **Home / End:** First / last item
- [ ] **Type a letter:** Jump to an item
- [ ] **Enter / Space:** Choose the item
- [ ] **Escape:** Close and return focus to the trigger
- [ ] **Tab:** Close

### Context menu (`<focsd-context-menu>`)

Pattern: Menu.

- [ ] Opens at the pointer on right-click or long press, or at the target with Shift+F10 or the ContextMenu key when the target has focus.
- [ ] Same menu semantics and keys as `focsd-menu`. Always provide another way to reach the same actions.
- [ ] **Shift + F10 / ContextMenu:** Open
- [ ] **Arrow Up / Down:** Move
- [ ] **Enter / Space:** Choose the item
- [ ] **Escape:** Close

### Alert dialog (`<focsd-alert-dialog>`)

Pattern: Alert dialog.

- [ ] `requestClose()` and `closedby` work as on `focsd-dialog`; keep the default `closedby` so Escape still cancels.
- [ ] `role="alertdialog"`, described by its body so the consequence is read with the title.
- [ ] Initial focus goes to `data-autofocus` (put it on the least destructive action), otherwise the first focusable element.
- [ ] The destructive action names its object ("Delete Atlas").
- [ ] **Tab:** Moves focus within the dialog; the page behind is inert
- [ ] **Escape:** Closes (cancels)

### Drawer / sheet (`<focsd-drawer>`)

Pattern: Dialog (modal, edge).

- [ ] `showModal()`, `requestClose()` and `closedby` work as on `focsd-dialog`.
- [ ] A modal dialog anchored to `end` (default), `start` or `bottom`, with the same focus behavior as `focsd-dialog`, including its close (×) button (`no-close` hides it).
- [ ] The slide animation is off under reduced motion.
- [ ] **Escape:** Closes

### Command palette (`<focsd-command>`)

Pattern: Dialog + combobox.

- [ ] A modal `<dialog>` with a combobox that filters a listbox of commands, grouped with named `role="group"`s.
- [ ] Arrow order always matches the order on screen.
- [ ] Focus returns to the element that was focused before opening.
- [ ] The `shortcut="mod+k"` attribute is opt-in, so it never clashes with page shortcuts by default.
- [ ] **⌘/Ctrl + K:** Toggle (with `shortcut="mod+k"`)
- [ ] **Arrow Up / Down:** Move through commands (wraps around)
- [ ] **Home / End:** First / last command
- [ ] **Enter:** Run the command (fires `focsd-select`) and close
- [ ] **Escape:** Close

### Floating panel (`<focsd-floating-panel>`)

Pattern: Non-modal dialog, draggable, keyboard move (WCAG 2.5.7).

- [ ] A non-modal `role="dialog"` named by `label`; the page stays usable while it is open, and the trigger gets `aria-expanded`.
- [ ] Dragging has a keyboard alternative (WCAG 2.5.7): the move button moves the panel with the arrow keys.
- [ ] The panel always stays fully on screen, including when the window is resized, and remembers where it was moved.
- [ ] Several panels can be open at once; the one you click or focus comes to the front.
- [ ] **Enter / Space (trigger):** Open or close
- [ ] **Arrow keys (move button):** Move 10px
- [ ] **Shift + arrow keys (move button):** Move 50px
- [ ] **Escape:** Close and return focus to the trigger

### Hover card (`<focsd-hover-card>`)

Pattern: Non-modal popover on hover/focus, hoverable and dismissible (1.4.13).

- [ ] Opens on hover after a delay and on keyboard focus; stays open while the pointer or focus is on the trigger or the card; Escape closes it without moving focus (WCAG 1.4.13).
- [ ] The card follows the trigger in focus order, so Tab moves into it, and leaving with Tab closes it.
- [ ] The trigger is described by the card text and reports `aria-expanded`.
- [ ] On touch, a tap follows the link and a long press opens the card.
- [ ] Never put the only way to reach something in a hover card: keep the same content reachable elsewhere.
- [ ] **Tab:** Focus the trigger (opens), then move into the card
- [ ] **Escape:** Close the card, keep focus

### Bottom sheet (`<focsd-bottom-sheet>`)

Pattern: Modal dialog or region at the bottom edge, snap points, keyboard resize.

- [ ] Modal by default: a native dialog named by `label`, with a focus trap, an inert page, Escape, and focus back on the opener.
- [ ] With `non-modal` it is a named region and the page stays usable.
- [ ] The handle is a slider ("Resize sheet", "40% of the screen"); arrow keys, Home, End, Enter and Space change the height, and a Close button closes it, so dragging is never required (WCAG 2.5.7).
- [ ] A drag that starts in scrolled content scrolls it; only a pull from the top moves the sheet. A downward flick dismisses.
- [ ] Respects the iPhone home indicator area (`env(safe-area-inset-bottom)`) and reduced motion.
- [ ] **Up / Down (handle):** Next or previous height
- [ ] **Left / Right (handle):** Same as Down / Up
- [ ] **Home / End (handle):** Lowest / highest height
- [ ] **Enter / Space (handle):** Cycle heights
- [ ] **Escape:** Close (modal)

### Tour (`<focsd-tour>`)

Pattern: Non-modal dialog anchored to each step's target.

- [ ] Each step is a non-modal dialog (`aria-modal="false"`) named by its title and described by its body, so the page stays usable: the spotlight never takes pointer events.
- [ ] Focus moves to each step's heading, so the title and body are read; the end of the tour returns focus to the element focused at `start()` (pass the opener as `start(index, opener)`: Safari does not focus a clicked button, so opening with the `open` attribute has no opener there).
- [ ] The progress ("Step 1 of 2") counts the steps whose targets are on the page when the tour starts. A step whose target is missing when reached is skipped and announced by its title ("Skipped “Filters”: it is not on this page."), or by its number when it has no title; a target removed while its step shows moves the tour on.
- [ ] Escape ends the tour unless `persistent` is set, or unless something in the page already handled it (a popup inside the page closing first); Skip tour always does. `close` fires either way: read `completed` to tell Finish from a dismissal. `focsd-step-change` fires with `detail.step` on every step.
- [ ] The target is scrolled into view, instantly under reduced motion.
- [ ] **Tab / Shift+Tab:** Move between Back, Next (or Finish) and Skip tour, and on into the page
- [ ] **Enter / Space:** Activate the focused button
- [ ] **Escape:** End the tour (unless `persistent` is set)

### Toggletip (`<focsd-toggletip>`)

Pattern: Button + non-modal popover, announced politely.

- [ ] Unlike `focsd-tooltip`, a toggletip opens on click, so it works on touch screens, and its note may hold links: they follow the button in Tab order.
- [ ] The button is named "More information" unless you set `label`; name it after what it explains when a page has several. It reports `aria-expanded` and is at least 24 by 24 pixels.
- [ ] Opening it leaves focus on the button and copies the note’s text into a polite status region, so a screen reader reads it without moving there.
- [ ] Escape, clicking the button again or clicking anywhere else closes it. If focus was on a link inside, it returns to the button.
- [ ] The element fires `focsd-open` when the note opens and `close` when it closes.
- [ ] **Enter / Space:** Open or close the note
- [ ] **Tab:** Move to a link inside the open note
- [ ] **Escape:** Close the note; focus stays on the button

### Lightbox (`<focsd-lightbox>`)

Pattern: Modal dialog + image gallery.

- [ ] The thumbnails are ordinary links to the full-size pictures, so without JavaScript each one opens its picture. A click with a modifier key, or a middle click, keeps its normal meaning.
- [ ] The viewer is a native modal dialog named by `label` (default "Image viewer"): the page behind is inert and Escape closes it. Focus returns to the thumbnail that opened it.
- [ ] Focus starts on Next (or on Close when there is one picture), so the arrow keys and Enter work at once.
- [ ] Each change is announced politely, for example "Image 2 of 4, Hills near the coast". The counter and the caption describe the dialog.
- [ ] Every picture needs `alt` text: the viewer shows it, and a missing one is warned about. Captions come from a `figcaption`.
- [ ] Previous and Next wrap at the ends, so the counter tells you where you are. The slide fades in by opacity only, and not at all under reduced motion.
- [ ] Swipe horizontally on a touch screen (at least 40 px) to move between pictures. The buttons are 44 px targets and the chevrons mirror in right-to-left text.
- [ ] **Enter:** Open the viewer from a thumbnail
- [ ] **Arrow Left / Right:** Previous / next picture (swapped in right-to-left text)
- [ ] **Home / End:** First / last picture
- [ ] **Escape:** Close and return to the thumbnail

### Notification center (`<focsd-notification-center>`)

Pattern: Non-modal popover dialog + list.

- [ ] The bell is a button named "Notifications, 3 unread" (the count is in its name, and the visible badge is hidden from assistive technology). With `label="Alerts"` it reads "Alerts, 3 unread".
- [ ] It opens a non-modal panel: the page stays usable, Escape closes it and returns focus to the bell, and a click outside closes it too.
- [ ] The list is a real list. An unread item has a visible dot and a visually hidden "unread" before its title, so unread is never only a color. The time reads as relative text ("2 minutes ago") and the exact time is in a `time` element.
- [ ] New notifications that arrive while the page is open are announced politely, together, after a 2 second window ("2 new notifications"), so a burst does not interrupt a screen reader. The first list is never announced; if the center starts empty and fills from a fetch, set `loaded` once that list is in, so the first notification to arrive after it is announced too.
- [ ] The app owns the data. The center fires `focsd-read` (with `ids`) and `focsd-dismiss` (with `id`); answer by setting `notifications` again. Nothing changes on its own.
- [ ] A notification with `href` makes its title a link, and following it marks it read. "Mark all as read" covers the rest. Without notifications the panel says so.
- [ ] Only `http:`, `https:`, `mailto:`, relative and `#fragment` hrefs become links. Any other (such as `javascript:` or `data:`) is dropped and the title shows as plain text, so a list from a server or from users cannot run script. Titles and bodies are always text, never markup.
- [ ] A `tone` is also a shape and a word: critical, caution and positive notifications show an icon and are read as "Error", "Warning" or "Success" before the title. The color bar is only a bonus.
- [ ] The first list the center shows is never announced as new: set the notifications once they load, and only later arrivals are announced (one message per two seconds).
- [ ] On narrow screens the panel is fixed to the bottom of the viewport so it never runs off the edge. It is not a draggable sheet.
- [ ] **Enter / Space:** Open or close the panel from the bell
- [ ] **Tab:** Move through Mark all as read, links and Dismiss buttons
- [ ] **Escape:** Close the panel and return focus to the bell

From markup:

- [ ] `focsd-notification` draws nothing itself: its attributes (`title`, `body`, `time`, `tone`, `href`, `read`) are the data the center reads.
- [ ] `max` caps the badge: with `max="9"` ten or more unread show as "9+", and the button name still says the real count.

## Navigation

### Tabs (`<focsd-tabs>`)

Pattern: Tabs.

- [ ] APG tabs with automatic activation: `role="tablist"`, `tab` and `tabpanel`, with `aria-selected`, `aria-controls` and `aria-labelledby` set on the hosts.
- [ ] One tab stop for the tab list; disabled tabs are skipped; arrows are mirrored in right-to-left pages.
- [ ] **Arrow Left / Right:** Previous / next tab (selects it)
- [ ] **Home / End:** First / last tab
- [ ] **Tab:** Move into the active panel

### Skip link (`<focsd-skip-link>`)

Pattern: Skip link.

- [ ] Hidden until focused, then shown in the top start corner above everything else. Make it the first element in `<body>`.
- [ ] Activating it moves focus to the target, adding `tabindex="-1"` when the target has none.
- [ ] With the default `href="#main"` and no element with that id, it focuses the main landmark of the first `focsd-app-shell` in the document. A shell inside another component's shadow root is not found, and with two shells the first wins; give your main an id and point `href` at it instead.
- [ ] **Tab (first):** Reveal
- [ ] **Enter:** Jump to the target

### Breadcrumb (`<focsd-breadcrumb>`)

Pattern: Breadcrumb.

- [ ] A `<nav aria-label="Breadcrumb">` landmark around an ordered list.
- [ ] The current item has `aria-current="page"` and is plain text; separators are hidden from screen readers.

### Pagination (`<focsd-pagination>`)

Pattern: Navigation landmark.

- [ ] A `<nav aria-label="Pagination">` landmark. Page buttons are named "Page 5"; the current one has `aria-current="page"`.
- [ ] Previous/next are named "Previous page"/"Next page" and disabled at the ends. Ellipses are hidden.
- [ ] With `href="/results?page={page}"` it renders real links; otherwise buttons that fire `focsd-page-change` with `detail.page`.

### Navigation menu (`<focsd-nav-menu>`)

Pattern: Disclosure navigation.

- [ ] APG disclosure navigation: groups are `<button aria-expanded>` that show their links; there is no `role="menu"`, so links behave like links.
- [ ] Opening one group closes the others; Escape closes and returns focus to its button; moving focus out closes it.
- [ ] **Enter / Space:** Open or close a group
- [ ] **Escape:** Close the open group
- [ ] **Tab:** Move through links

### Sidebar (`<focsd-sidebar>`)

Pattern: Navigation landmark + collapse.

- [ ] A `<nav aria-label>` landmark with a collapse `<button aria-expanded>`; its name stays "Collapse sidebar" while the state changes.
- [ ] When collapsed, item labels stay available as accessible names.

### Menubar (`<focsd-menubar>`)

Pattern: Menubar.

- [ ] APG menubar: `role="menubar"` with one tab stop; each item is a `role="menuitem"` with `aria-haspopup="menu"` and `aria-expanded`.
- [ ] Use only for application-style commands. For site navigation use `focsd-nav-menu`.
- [ ] **Arrow Left / Right:** Move between menus (and switch the open menu)
- [ ] **Enter / Space / Arrow Down:** Open at the first item
- [ ] **Arrow Up:** Open at the last item
- [ ] **Escape:** Close and return focus

### Stepper (`<focsd-stepper>`)

Pattern: List with current step.

- [ ] A `role="list"` of steps, named by `label`; the current step has `aria-current="step"`.
- [ ] Each step carries visually hidden status text ("Completed", "Current step", "Not started"), so state is never shown by color alone.

### Header / top bar (`<focsd-header>`)

Pattern: Banner landmark.

- [ ] A `<header role="banner">` landmark: use one per page, at the top level (not inside `<main>`).
- [ ] Below `collapse-below` pixels (default 768) a "Menu" button with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` shows and hides the navigation; slotted `focsd-nav-menu`s switch to a vertical layout whose groups open in place.
- [ ] Escape closes the menu and returns focus to the button; following a link closes it.
- [ ] `sticky` keeps the header at the top while scrolling. Make sure focused elements are never hidden behind it (WCAG 2.4.11): add `scroll-padding-top` equal to its height.
- [ ] **Enter / Space (Menu):** Open or close the navigation
- [ ] **Escape:** Close and return focus to Menu

### Footer (`<focsd-footer>`)

Pattern: Contentinfo landmark + link sections.

- [ ] A `<footer role="contentinfo">` landmark: use one per page, at the top level.
- [ ] Each `focsd-footer-section` is a navigation landmark named by its heading (level 2 by default; set `level` to fit your outline), so screen-reader users can jump between link groups.
- [ ] Sections wrap into a responsive grid; links keep a 24px minimum target.

### Table of contents (`<focsd-table-of-contents>`)

Pattern: Nav of links with aria-current="location".

- [ ] It renders a navigation landmark named "On this page"; set `label` when a page has more than one.
- [ ] It lists the `h2` and `h3` headings of the first element matching `for` (by default `main`, or `focsd-app-shell`). Set `levels` to choose others, such as `levels="2"`. An `h3` is nested in a list under the `h2` before it.
- [ ] A heading without an `id` gets one made from its text, so its link and the address bar point at it.
- [ ] The link of the section in view has `aria-current="location"`, which screen readers read as "current location".
- [ ] Following a link scrolls to the heading (without animation when reduced motion is preferred), moves focus to it and adds its `#id` to the address, so Back returns to where you were.
- [ ] Put your own links (`a[href^="#"]`) inside to replace the generated list; the current section is still marked on them.
- [ ] **Tab:** Move between links
- [ ] **Enter:** Go to the heading and focus it

### Bottom navigation (`<focsd-bottom-nav>`)

Pattern: Navigation landmark (links).

- [ ] A navigation landmark named "Main" (set `label` for another name) holding real links. Open in a new tab, copy the address and modifier clicks all work, and without JavaScript each one still goes to its page.
- [ ] The current item has `aria-current="page"`, and is shown with a heavier label and a bar above it, so it is never only a color. In forced colors it gets an outline.
- [ ] A `badge` joins the link's name, so a screen reader hears "Inbox, 3 new", not a bare 3. The visible badge is hidden from assistive technology.
- [ ] Items are at least 48 px wide and tall. On a phone with a home indicator the bar pads itself by the safe-area inset.
- [ ] Use three to five items. Fewer or more logs a warning, because more than five crowds the targets.
- [ ] It shows below 768 px by default and hides on wider screens (`hide-above`, in px; 0 never hides). Give wider screens a sidebar or a header navigation instead.
- [ ] Fixed to the bottom by default, the element keeps the bar's height in the page, so the last of your content is never covered. `position="sticky"` and `"static"` are the alternatives.
- [ ] Place the bar last in the page, after all other content. Placed first, the space it keeps is at the top and the bar covers the last content.
- [ ] A fixed bar covers what scrolls under it, so a focused element could end up hidden behind it (WCAG 2.4.11). Set `scroll-padding-block-end` on `html` to the bar's height: `calc(var(--focsd-bottom-nav-height, 4rem) + env(safe-area-inset-bottom))`. The component cannot set it from inside its shadow root.
- [ ] To use a client-side router, register it once with `setLinkHandler`, as in [the router recipes](/foundations/utilities/).
- [ ] **Tab:** Move between the links
- [ ] **Enter:** Follow the focused link

## Disclosure

### Accordion (`<focsd-accordion>`)

Pattern: Accordion.

- [ ] Items with the same `name` form an exclusive group, like `<details name>` (the accordion does this for its own items unless `multiple`).
- [ ] Each item renders a heading (level from `level`, default 3) wrapping a `<button aria-expanded aria-controls>`, and a `role="region"` panel labeled by the button.
- [ ] Set `multiple` to allow several open items.
- [ ] **Enter / Space:** Toggle the section
- [ ] **Arrow Up / Down:** Previous / next header (wrapping)
- [ ] **Home / End:** First / last header

### Disclosure (`<focsd-disclosure>`)

Pattern: Disclosure (details).

- [ ] `name` makes disclosures in the same tree an exclusive group: opening one closes the others, like `<details name>`.
- [ ] A `<button aria-expanded aria-controls>` and its panel in one shadow root.
- [ ] Fires `toggle` when it opens or closes.
- [ ] **Enter / Space:** Toggle

## Data

### Table (`<focsd-table>`)

Pattern: Table (sortable headers).

- [ ] A native `<table>` with `<caption>` and `th scope="col"`; sortable headers contain a button and the `th` carries `aria-sort`.
- [ ] The wrapper is a labeled scroll region that becomes focusable when the table overflows, so wide tables can be scrolled with the keyboard.

### Data grid (`<focsd-data-grid>`)

Pattern: Grid (sort, filter, paginate, virtualize).

- [ ] APG grid (or treegrid when grouped) with `aria-rowcount`, `aria-colcount`, `aria-rowindex` and `aria-colindex` that stay correct under paging, windowing, pinning and hidden columns.
- [ ] One tab stop for all cells. Pinned columns are sticky cells inside each row, so every row is still one row to assistive technology.
- [ ] Sorting, filtering, grouping, selection, edits and column changes are announced in a polite live region ("Sorted by Amount, descending", "Filter applied: Region is Europe. 14 of 40 rows").
- [ ] Every pointer gesture has a keyboard path: the column menu resizes (Widen, Narrow, Autosize), pins and hides; the Columns panel shows, hides and reorders.
- [ ] Editors are labeled ("Edit Amount"); invalid input keeps the editor open with an error that is described and announced.
- [ ] **Arrow keys:** Move between cells
- [ ] **Home / End:** First / last cell in the row
- [ ] **Ctrl + Home / End:** First / last cell in the grid
- [ ] **Page Up / Down:** Previous / next page, or a screen of rows when not paginated
- [ ] **Enter (header):** Sort; Shift + Enter adds to the sort
- [ ] **Alt + Arrow Down / Shift + F10 / Menu (header):** Open the column menu
- [ ] **Space:** Select the row; Shift + Space selects a range
- [ ] **Ctrl / ⌘ + A:** Select all rows (`selection="multiple"`)
- [ ] **Enter / F2 / typing:** Edit the cell (Enter saves and moves down, Tab saves and moves sideways, Escape cancels)
- [ ] **Enter (read-only cell):** Fire `focsd-row-activate`
- [ ] **Enter / Space / Arrow Right / Arrow Left (group row):** Toggle, expand or collapse the group (arrows in the first column)

### Tree view (`<focsd-tree>`)

Pattern: Tree.

- [ ] APG tree view: `role="tree"`, items are `role="treeitem"` with `aria-level`, `aria-expanded` (parents only) and `aria-selected`.
- [ ] One tab stop. If the focused item is hidden because a parent collapses (for example from code), focus moves to the nearest visible parent, so it is never lost.
- [ ] **Arrow Up / Down:** Previous / next visible item
- [ ] **Arrow Right:** Expand, or move to the first child
- [ ] **Arrow Left:** Collapse, or move to the parent
- [ ] **Home / End:** First / last item
- [ ] **Enter / Space:** Select
- [ ] **Type a letter:** Jump to an item

### Virtual list (`<focsd-virtual-list>`)

Pattern: List or listbox rendering only visible rows, setsize/posinset.

- [ ] Rows carry `aria-setsize` and `aria-posinset`, so screen readers announce "item 4,051 of 100,000".
- [ ] The scrolling area is focusable, so keyboard users can scroll it.
- [ ] With `selectable="single"` or `"multiple"` it is an APG listbox with `aria-activedescendant`, Shift ranges and Ctrl/⌘ + A.
- [ ] Rows that grow above the view (images loading) keep what you are reading in place.
- [ ] **Arrow Up / Down:** Move the active row (listbox); with `selectable="single"` the row is also selected
- [ ] **Home / End:** First / last row (listbox)
- [ ] **Page Up / Page Down:** Move by a page (listbox), or scroll
- [ ] **Space / Enter:** Toggle the active row (listbox)
- [ ] **Shift + Arrow Up / Down, Home, End, Page Up / Down:** Extend the selection (multiple)
- [ ] **Ctrl / ⌘ + A:** Select all, or clear when all are selected (multiple)

## Charts

### Chart (`<focsd-chart>`)

Pattern: Figure + data table + keyboard-explorable points.

- [ ] A figure named by its caption and described by a generated summary ("Bar chart, 4 categories, 2 series. Highest: Online, Q4, $2,100."), or your own `description`.
- [ ] Data points are one tab stop: arrow keys move between categories (left and right) and series (up and down), Home and End jump to the ends, and each point is named "Series, category: value".
- [ ] The Show data table button reveals the same numbers as a real table with row and column headers.
- [ ] Series differ by pattern and marker shape as well as color, so the chart works in grayscale and for color-blind readers.
- [ ] Values are formatted with `Intl.NumberFormat` (`format` property) in the page language.
- [ ] Set `type` to `area` or `scatter`, add `stacked` to bars or areas, and `mirror` to flip the horizontal direction. See [the charts guide](/guides/charts/) for each type.
- [ ] **Tab:** Move to the chart, then to the table button
- [ ] **Arrow Left / Right:** Previous / next category
- [ ] **Arrow Up / Down:** Previous / next series
- [ ] **Home / End:** First / last category in the series

### Sparkline (`<focsd-sparkline>`)

Pattern: Image (role=img) named by a generated sentence.

- [ ] An image named by its `label` and a generated sentence: "Signups per day: 6 values, from 4 to 19, last 17, up 325% from the first". The words are localized like every other component.
- [ ] It has no focusable points and is not a tab stop. When the detail matters, use a [chart](/components/chart/) with its data table.
- [ ] It is drawn at the size of the text (`--focsd-sparkline-height`, `--focsd-sparkline-width`), in one color. Forced colors use the system text color.
- [ ] Empty data is named "No data"; non-numbers are skipped.

### Gauge (`<focsd-gauge>`)

Pattern: Meter (role=meter) with named bands.

- [ ] A `meter` named by its `label`, with `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax` and `aria-valuenow`. The value text includes the current band, such as "72%, Warning", so no meaning is carried by color.
- [ ] The bands are also a visible list ("Normal, up to 60%"), with the current band marked, so the dial is not the only way to read them.
- [ ] The value is kept inside `min` and `max`; a `max` that is not above `min` falls back to `min + 1`. A missing `label` warns once in the console.
- [ ] There is no animation. Forced colors draw every shape in the system text color.

## Display

### Badge (`<focsd-badge>`)

Pattern: Static.

- [ ] Plain inline text: the words carry the meaning, the tone color only reinforces it.

Indicator:

- [ ] With `dot` or `count`, the default slot is the anchor (an avatar or icon) and the badge draws an indicator on one of its corners.
- [ ] The indicator is hidden from screen readers. Visually hidden text says the same thing: the count and the `label` ("3 unread"), or the dot’s `label` ("Online"). Inside a link or button it becomes part of the name, with a space on each side, such as "Inbox 3 unread" or "120 unread Messages".
- [ ] The visible count stops at `max` (99 by default, shown as "99+"); the hidden text keeps the real number.
- [ ] A `count` of 0 shows the anchor alone and adds nothing to the name.
- [ ] A dot needs a `label`; without one it is decorative, adds nothing to the name, and the badge warns once in the console, because a colored dot means nothing to a screen reader.
- [ ] `placement` picks the corner: `top-end` (the default), `top-start`, `bottom-end` or `bottom-start`. Start and end follow the reading direction, so `top-end` is top left in right-to-left text.
- [ ] The count is dark text on a light red tint with a red edge; the dot is solid red with a ring in the surface color. Both stay visible in forced colors.

### Tag / chip (`<focsd-tag>`)

Pattern: Static + optional remove button.

- [ ] The label names the tag; the icon is decoration and hidden from assistive technology, so a status always reads in words, never by color or icon alone.
- [ ] A toned tag is filled with its tone and edged in it. Tones are `neutral` (default), `info`, `positive`, `caution` and `critical`.
- [ ] When `removable`, a real button named "Remove Design" fires `focsd-remove`; the tag does not remove itself, so your app stays in control (and can move focus sensibly).
- [ ] **Enter / Space (remove button):** Fire `focsd-remove`

Category colors:

- [ ] The color only groups tags visually; the label carries the meaning, so nothing is lost without color (WCAG 1.4.1).

Sizes and shapes:

- [ ] The remove button stays at least 24 px at every size (WCAG 2.5.8 target size).

### Card (`<focsd-card>`)

Pattern: Static (article/section).

- [ ] A plain container with no landmark or `article` role; wrap it in `<article>` yourself when the card is a self-contained item.
- [ ] Do not nest cards.

### Avatar (`<focsd-avatar>`)

Pattern: Img with text fallback.

- [ ] `role="img"` named by `name`; falls back to initials when there is no image or it fails.
- [ ] Add `decorative` when the name is already shown next to it.

### Avatar group (`<focsd-avatar-group>`)

Pattern: List.

- [ ] A labeled `role="group"`; avatars over `max` collapse into "+2", announced as "2 more".

### Kbd (`<focsd-kbd>`)

Pattern: Static.

- [ ] Renders a native `<kbd>`.

### List (`<focsd-list>`)

Pattern: List / listbox (selectable).

- [ ] Static: `role="list"` and `listitem`.
- [ ] Selectable: a labeled `role="listbox"` of `option`s with `aria-selected`, one tab stop, firing `change`.
- [ ] **Arrow Up / Down:** Move (selectable)
- [ ] **Home / End:** First / last item
- [ ] **Enter / Space:** Select

Sortable:

- [ ] Each item has a "Reorder {item}" button before its content. Grabbing, each move, the drop and a cancel are announced politely ("Grabbed Design review, position 2 of 5", "Moved to position 3 of 5", "Dropped at position 3"). When an item holds other controls, such as a menu button, or its text changes after it is shown, set its `label` so the handle and announcements use that name and not all of its text.
- [ ] The handle keeps focus while the item moves. A click elsewhere or focus leaving the list puts a grabbed item back.
- [ ] Dragging the handle with a mouse or a finger lifts the item, shows a dashed placeholder where it will land, and scrolls a scrolling container near its edges.
- [ ] The list fires a cancelable `focsd-reorder` with `detail.from`, `detail.to` and `detail.item`; cancel it to put the item back. Otherwise the list moves the item element itself.
- [ ] A disabled item cannot be moved: its handle is disabled.
- [ ] A list that is both `selectable` and `sortable` puts no button inside its options (an option may not hold one). The handle is for a mouse or a finger only and is hidden from screen readers; Alt + Arrow Up or Down moves the focused option one place and announces "Moved to position 2 of 5".
- [ ] **Space / Enter (on a handle):** Grab the item, or drop it
- [ ] **Arrow Up / Down:** Move the grabbed item one place
- [ ] **Escape:** Put the item back where it was
- [ ] **Tab:** Drop the item and move on
- [ ] **Alt + Arrow Up / Down:** Move the focused option one place (selectable and sortable)

### Description list (`<focsd-description-list>`)

Pattern: dl.

- [ ] Each item renders a valid `<dl><dt>term</dt><dd>value</dd></dl>` group, so screen readers announce term and value together.

### Timeline (`<focsd-timeline>`)

Pattern: Ordered list.

- [ ] A list of items, each with a machine-readable `<time datetime>` and its heading text. Markers are decorative.

### Code block (`<focsd-code>`)

Pattern: Pre/code + copy button.

- [ ] The `<pre>` is a focusable, labeled region so long lines can be scrolled with the keyboard.
- [ ] "Copy code" announces "Copied" in a polite live region. If copying fails, it announces "Copy failed" and selects the code so it can be copied by hand.

### Image / aspect ratio (`<focsd-image>`)

Pattern: Img with ratio + fallback.

- [ ] `srcset`, `sizes`, `width` and `height` (which also reserve the aspect ratio), `loading` (default `lazy`), `decoding`, `fetchpriority`, `crossorigin` and `referrerpolicy` are forwarded; `complete`, `naturalWidth`, `naturalHeight` and `decode()` work as on a native image.
- [ ] `alt` is required: describe the image, or use `alt=""` for decorative images.
- [ ] If loading fails, the fallback panel keeps the description (`role="img"` with `aria-label`).
- [ ] Loads lazily and decodes asynchronously by default.

### Carousel (`<focsd-carousel>`)

Pattern: Carousel (pause, prev/next).

- [ ] APG carousel: a labeled region with `aria-roledescription="carousel"`; slides are groups named "1 of 3". Hidden slides are `inert`.
- [ ] With `autoplay`, a Stop/Start rotation button appears; rotation pauses while hovered or focused and starts paused under reduced motion.
- [ ] Slide changes are announced politely except while rotating.

### QR code (`<focsd-qr-code>`)

Pattern: SVG image (role=img).

- [ ] The code is one image named by `label`. Say where the code leads ("QR code for focsd.dev") rather than "QR code"; the element warns once in the console when `label` is missing.
- [ ] Show the link or text next to the code too: not everyone can scan one.
- [ ] Colors follow the theme, so dark themes draw a light-on-dark (reversed) code, which some scanners refuse. For print or scanning set `--focsd-qr-code-ink: #000; --focsd-qr-code-surface: #fff`.
- [ ] Pages with a strict style policy (no inline styles) set `--focsd-qr-code-ink` and `--focsd-qr-code-surface` in a stylesheet rather than a `style` attribute.
- [ ] In forced colors the code stays black on white, since a code drawn in system colors may not scan.
- [ ] A value too long for any QR code draws an empty image that keeps its name and fires `focsd-error` with `detail.reason` `too-long`.

### Stat (`<focsd-stat>`)

Pattern: Group named by its label; the change in words.
