- [ ] A group named by its `label`. The value, then the change, are read as words: "Up 12.4% from last month, good". An arrow is only decoration.
- [ ] The change is never carried by color alone: the direction is in the words, and the good or bad judgement is visible text, not only a green or red tint.
- [ ] `delta` is a fraction under the default `delta-format` (0.12 is 12%); the sign sets the direction unless `trend` is set. `good="down"` marks a fall as good news, for costs or churn.
- [ ] `value` can be a number or any text. Format numbers with `format`: a short form (`currency USD`, `currency EUR 0`, `percent 1`, `compact`, `unit kilometer`, `decimal 2`, where a trailing number is the most decimals), JSON for any other `Intl.NumberFormat` options, or a property.
- [ ] With `href`, the label is a link.

Counting up:

- [ ] The counting text is hidden from screen readers; a visually hidden copy holds the final value, so nothing is read out while the digits change.
- [ ] Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the value changes at once, with no counting.
- [ ] The property is `animated` (the attribute is `animate`), because every element already has an `animate()` method.

### Status dot (`<focsd-status-dot>`)

Pattern: Image (role=img): a shape per status, named by its label.

- [ ] Every status has its own shape (filled, ring, bar, triangle, cross, dash) as well as its own color, so it works in grayscale and for color-blind readers.
- [ ] It is an image named by its status ("Online"). A custom `label` goes first and the status stays in the name ("Disk almost full, Warning"), so assistive technology always hears the status. Without `label-visible` the name is only read.
- [ ] Unknown statuses fall back to neutral, named "Unknown".
- [ ] `pulse` adds a slow halo to an online dot. It beats twice (about 4 seconds) and stops, so it never runs for more than 5 seconds. It is hidden under reduced motion and in forced colors, and it only animates `transform` and `opacity`.
- [ ] In forced colors every shape is drawn in the system text color, so the shape alone carries the status.

### Image compare (`<focsd-image-compare>`)

Pattern: Slider (window splitter).

- [ ] The divider handle is a slider (`role="slider"`) from 0 to 100, with the value said in words: "60% before image". Both pictures' `alt` texts are in its description, so a screen reader hears what each side shows.
- [ ] The before image sits on the inline-start side (left in left-to-right text, right in right-to-left), and the slider value is how much of the before image shows.
- [ ] Dragging works anywhere on the figure, not only on the handle, and a drag moves focus to the handle. `focsd-position-change` fires once at the end of a drag and on each key press.
- [ ] Give both pictures real `alt` text. A missing `alt` is warned about once, because the slider has nothing to describe without it.
- [ ] With `orientation="vertical"` the divider is horizontal and the before image is on top.
- [ ] **Arrow keys:** Move the divider by 1 (Left and Right swap in right-to-left text)
- [ ] **Shift + arrow / Page Up / Page Down:** Move the divider by 10
- [ ] **Home / End:** Show all of the after image / all of the before image

Vertical:

- [ ] Up and Right arrows raise the value and Down and Left lower it, as for any slider (APG), so the divider moves down when you press Up. The value is how much of the before image shows.

## Feedback

### Alert / banner (`<focsd-alert>`)

Pattern: Alert / status.

- [ ] Static by default. Set `live="polite"` (`role="status"`) or `live="assertive"` (`role="alert"`) only when the alert appears in response to something.
- [ ] Tone always comes with an icon and a headline in words, never color alone.
- [ ] `closable` adds a close (×) button named "Close". It fires a cancelable `close` (it does not bubble), then hides the alert; cancel it to keep the alert or to remove it yourself.

### Skeleton (`<focsd-skeleton>`)

Pattern: aria-busy placeholder.

- [ ] Hidden from assistive technology (`aria-hidden`). Mark the loading container with `aria-busy="true"` and announce completion if it matters.
- [ ] The shimmer stops under reduced motion.

### Spinner (`<focsd-spinner>`)

Pattern: Status (polite).

- [ ] A polite `role="status"` named by `label` (default "Loading").
- [ ] Under reduced motion it pulses instead of rotating.
- [ ] `size` picks a preset: `s` (16px), `m` (24px, the default), `l` (40px) or `xl` (56px). For any other size set `--focsd-spinner-size`; the ring's thickness follows it. `--focsd-spinner-color` and `--focsd-spinner-track` set its colors.

### Progress bar (`<focsd-progress>`)

Pattern: Progressbar.

- [ ] `role="progressbar"` with `aria-valuenow/min/max` and a required `label`; indeterminate omits `aria-valuenow`.

Ring:

- [ ] The ring is the same `role="progressbar"` as the bar, named by `label`, with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin` and `aria-valuemax`; the drawing is hidden from assistive technology.
- [ ] With `show-value` the percentage appears in the center. It is hidden from screen readers, which already read the value from `aria-valuenow`.
- [ ] While `indeterminate`, there is no `aria-valuenow` and the ring turns. When reduced motion is preferred it stops turning and shows a still arc.
- [ ] Like the bar, the track is a sunk band with a thin edge-colored outline on each side. The arc against the band measures 6.33:1 (light), 10.02:1 (dark) and 16.39:1 (contrast), and the outline against the page 3.63:1, 3.63:1 and 21:1, so both the value and the ring’s extent meet the 3:1 non-text minimum.
- [ ] In forced colors the arc uses `Highlight`, the band `Canvas` and its outlines `CanvasText`.
- [ ] Set `--focsd-progress-ring-size` to change its size (3rem by default).

### Meter (`<focsd-meter>`)

Pattern: Meter.

- [ ] `role="meter"` with `aria-valuetext`; the range color is backed by the value text, so color is not the only signal.
- [ ] Use progress for tasks, meter for measurements.

### Toast (`<focsd-toaster>`)

Pattern: Status / log region.

- [ ] The toaster is a polite `role="status"` live region that exists before toasts arrive, so every message is announced.
- [ ] Toasts never take focus. Timers pause while hovered or focused (WCAG 2.2.1); each toast has a "Dismiss notification" button.
- [ ] Do not put the only path to an action in a toast.

### Empty state (`<focsd-empty-state>`)

Pattern: Static.

- [ ] A real heading (level from `level`, default 2) so the state is discoverable by heading navigation.
- [ ] Not a live region: announce changes elsewhere if content disappears after an action.

### Loading overlay (`<focsd-loading-overlay>`)

Pattern: Busy, inert region + overlay with status.

- [ ] While `active`, the content is `inert` (no focus, no clicks, hidden from assistive technology) and marked `aria-busy`.
- [ ] "Loading" (or `label`) is announced when loading starts and "Loaded" when it ends, through a polite status region. When focus moves to the overlay, its name already says "Loading", so the status stays quiet until "Loaded".
- [ ] An overlay that is already `active` when it first renders neither announces nor moves focus; only later changes of `active` do.
- [ ] If focus was inside the content, it moves to the overlay while loading and comes back afterwards; if that element is gone, it goes to the first focusable element in the content. Focus elsewhere on the page is left alone.
- [ ] Use `label` to say what is happening ("Saving changes"); keep it short. For richer content, put an element with `slot="label"` inside (its text is announced), and `slot="indicator"` for your own image or animation in place of the spinner.
- [ ] No glue code for the common cases: `run(save)` shows it until `save()` settles, and `busy-on-submit` turns it on when a form inside posts to the server.
- [ ] In forced colors the overlay is an opaque system surface with an outline.

## Layout

### Separator (`<focsd-separator>`)

Pattern: Separator.

- [ ] `role="separator"` with `aria-orientation`; add `decorative` (`role="none"`) to hide purely visual dividers from assistive technology.
- [ ] Set the color with `--focsd-separator-color` (default the edge color, visible on every theme).

### Scroll area (`<focsd-scroll-area>`)

Pattern: Focusable scroll region.

- [ ] A focusable, labeled `role="region"`, so keyboard users can scroll it (WCAG 2.1.1).
- [ ] **Arrow keys / Page Up / Down:** Scroll (when focused)

### Splitter / resizable (`<focsd-splitter>`)

Pattern: Window splitter.

- [ ] APG window splitter: the divider is a focusable `role="separator"` with `aria-valuenow/min/max` and `aria-controls` pointing at the start pane.
- [ ] **Arrow keys:** Resize by 1% (10% with Shift)
- [ ] **Home / End:** Minimum / maximum
- [ ] **Enter:** Collapse or restore

Panes:

- [ ] Each boundary is an APG window splitter: a focusable `role="separator"` named "Resize <pane label>", with `aria-valuenow` (the size of the pane before it) and that pane’s `min` and `max` as `aria-valuemin` and `aria-valuemax`.
- [ ] Separators are vertical lines in a row of panes and horizontal lines with `orientation="vertical"`; `aria-orientation` says which.
- [ ] A collapsed pane is hidden (`display: none`), so its content leaves the tab order until it is restored.
- [ ] The visible line is thin, but the pointer target is 24 px wide.
- [ ] With `autosave`, the sizes are kept in `localStorage` under `focsd-splitter:<key>` and come back on the next visit. Splitters can be nested.
- [ ] Markup with `start` and `end` slots instead of panes keeps the two-pane behavior (`change` event).
- [ ] `orientation` is new and applies to panes only. It does not reflect, so style on `focsd-splitter[orientation=vertical]` only when you set the attribute, not the property.
- [ ] **Arrow keys:** Resize by 1% (Left and Right in a row, mirrored right to left; Up and Down in a column)
- [ ] **Shift + arrow keys:** Resize by 10%
- [ ] **Home / End:** The pane before the separator to its minimum / maximum
- [ ] **Enter:** Collapse or restore the collapsible pane beside the separator

### Masonry (`<focsd-masonry>`)

Pattern: Columns of varying height, DOM-order placement by default.

- [ ] Uses CSS masonry (`display: grid-lanes`) where the browser has it, and places items itself elsewhere.
- [ ] The default `order="dom"` keeps the visual order close to the reading and focus order (WCAG 1.3.2, 2.4.3).
- [ ] Where the browser has CSS masonry, it places each item in the shortest column itself, so `order` has no effect and the layout behaves like `order="balanced"`. If the visual order must follow the reading order everywhere, set `nativeMasonry = false`.
- [ ] `order="balanced"` packs tighter but can separate what is next to what visually from the focus order: use it only for items that do not need to be read in sequence.
- [ ] Children keep their own semantics; the container adds no role.

### App shell (`<focsd-app-shell>`)

Pattern: Landmarks grid + skip link + drawer below a width.

- [ ] The shell renders the page's one `main` landmark around its default slot; the header and footer keep their own banner and contentinfo landmarks, and the sidebar its navigation landmark.
- [ ] The first Tab stop is a "Skip to main content" link, hidden until focused. It moves focus to `main`.
- [ ] `main` scrolls on its own while the header and footer stay put. It is a tab stop, so keyboard users can scroll it even when it holds no links.
- [ ] Below `collapse-below` (768 pixels by default) the sidebar moves into a modal dialog named by `nav-label`, opened by an "Open navigation" button before the header. Escape, the close button or following a link closes it, and focus returns to the button.
- [ ] Put the content straight in the default slot: a `<main>` inside the shell would be a second main landmark, and the shell warns about it in the console.
- [ ] Right-to-left pages put the sidebar, and the drawer, on the right.
- [ ] **Tab:** The skip link first, then the header, sidebar, main and footer
- [ ] **Enter:** On the skip link: move focus to the main content
- [ ] **Escape:** Close the navigation drawer

## Utility

### Visually hidden (`<focsd-visually-hidden>`)

Pattern: SR-only.

- [ ] Hidden visually, still read. Becomes visible when focus is inside it.

### Icon (`<focsd-icon>`)

Pattern: Decorative / labeled img.

- [ ] Decorative (`aria-hidden`) by default; with `label` it becomes `role="img"` with that name.
- [ ] Bring your own icons with `registerIconLibrary`, or slot your own SVG. See [Icons](/foundations/icons/).
- [ ] `mirror` flips directional icons in right-to-left text.
- [ ] Uses `currentColor`, so it follows the text color in every theme.

### Format number (`<focsd-format-number>`)

Pattern: Data element (Intl.NumberFormat).

- [ ] The text sits in a `<data>` element whose `value` is the raw number, so scripts and machines can read the exact figure.
- [ ] Without `locale` it follows the nearest `lang` attribute, so the separators match the language around it and screen readers read it in that language.
- [ ] Write the unit in `unit` or `currency` rather than next to the number, so it is formatted and read together with it.
- [ ] It is plain inline text: it takes the surrounding font and color, and adds no role or focus stop.
- [ ] A value that is not a number shows nothing (and warns in the console), rather than "NaN".
- [ ] With `type="bytes"` the size is scaled to its unit first (kB, or KiB with `binary`), so `notation="compact"` changes nothing and `notation="scientific"` gives text such as "1.5E0 KiB". Leave `notation` at `standard` for sizes.

### Relative time (`<focsd-relative-time>`)

Pattern: Time element (Intl.RelativeTimeFormat).

- [ ] The text sits in a `<time>` element whose `datetime` is the exact moment, so scripts and machines can read it.
- [ ] The full date and time follows the relative text as visually hidden text, so a screen reader reads "3 minutes ago, October 15, 2026 at 10:41 AM". The same text is the tooltip.
- [ ] It has no live region: the text updates once a minute (once an hour for older times) without being announced, which would be noise.
- [ ] With `format="auto"`, times more than 7 days away show the date instead, which is easier to place than "3 weeks ago".
- [ ] Without `locale` it follows the nearest `lang` attribute. With `locale` the text carries that `lang`, so screen readers read it in that language.
- [ ] Server-rendered pages show the text for the moment the server rendered it; it corrects itself when the element loads in the browser.

### Theme toggle (`<focsd-theme-toggle>`)

Pattern: Radio group (light / dark / system).

- [ ] It is a radio group named "Color theme" (or `label`). Each option has visible text (Light, Dark, System, High contrast) beside its icon, so the choice never depends on the icon alone.
- [ ] The group is one Tab stop. The arrow keys move between the options and choose them, as in any radio group; Home and End go to the first and last. In right-to-left text, Left moves forward.
- [ ] The chosen option shows a border and a bar under it as well as a color change, and a Highlight border in forced-colors mode.
- [ ] System removes `data-focsd-theme`, so the page follows `prefers-color-scheme` (and `prefers-contrast`). The choice is stored as `focsd-theme` in `localStorage`; storage that is blocked is ignored.
- [ ] Put the tokens' `noFlashScript` in the page head so a returning visitor's theme applies before the first paint.
- [ ] **Tab:** Move to the chosen option
- [ ] **Arrow keys:** Move to the next or previous option and choose it
- [ ] **Home / End:** Choose the first or last option

### Theme picker (`<focsd-theme-picker>`)

Pattern: Radio group of preset swatch cards.

- [ ] It is a radio group named "Theme preset" (or `label`). Each card is a radio named by its text ("Harbor"); the first is "Wayfinding (default)", which removes the preset.
- [ ] The swatch (action, route and surface colors, in the current light or dark scheme) is decorative and hidden from assistive technology. The chosen card has a check mark and a heavier border, so the choice never depends on color.
- [ ] The group is one Tab stop; the arrow keys move between the cards and choose them, Home and End go to the first and last, and Left moves forward in right-to-left text.
- [ ] High contrast always wins: under `data-focsd-theme="contrast"` or `prefers-contrast: more` a preset keeps its type and corners but not its colors.
- [ ] The choice is stored as `focsd-brand` in `localStorage`; storage that is blocked is ignored.
- [ ] **Tab:** Move to the chosen card
- [ ] **Arrow keys:** Move to the next or previous card and choose it
- [ ] **Home / End:** Choose the first or last card

### Animated number (`<focsd-animated-number>`)

Pattern: Counting text (hidden) + visually hidden final value.

- [ ] The counting digits are hidden from assistive technology. A visually hidden copy of the final value is what is read, once, so a screen reader never hears 1,281, 1,282, 1,283.
- [ ] Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the text is the final value in the same frame: there is no counting.
- [ ] `format` takes a short form (`decimal 0`, `currency USD`, `percent 1`, `compact`) or `Intl.NumberFormat` options (JSON as an attribute); an invalid format warns once and falls back to the plain number. `from` sets where a count starts and `duration` how long it takes, in milliseconds.
- [ ] The change is not announced as a live region. If people need to hear it, announce it from your own code.

## AI

### Chat thread (`<focsd-chat-thread>`)

Pattern: Feed (APG) with a jump-to-latest button.

- [ ] The thread is `role="feed"` named by `label` (default "Conversation"; until the first message it is a named group, because a feed must hold articles); each message is an `article` with `aria-posinset` and `aria-setsize`, and the one that is streaming has `aria-busy="true"`.
- [ ] There is no live region on the feed. When a reply finishes, the thread announces "Assistant replied:" and its text once, politely, cut at the last word before 300 characters. A stopped reply says "Response stopped"; a failed one says the error, assertively. History set all at once is silent.
- [ ] It follows new content only while the reader is at the bottom. Scrolled up, a "Jump to latest" button appears; it scrolls down and moves focus to the latest message.
- [ ] The feed is one tab stop (the last focused message, at first the latest). Page Down and Page Up move between messages; Ctrl+Home and Ctrl+End leave the feed, as the APG feed pattern describes.
- [ ] Give it a chat controller with `thread.chat = createChat({ transport })` and it shows and follows the controller; retry calls `chat.retry(id)` unless a listener cancels `focsd-retry`.
- [ ] **Page Down:** Focus the next message
- [ ] **Page Up:** Focus the previous message
- [ ] **Ctrl+Home:** Focus the element before the feed
- [ ] **Ctrl+End:** Focus the element after the feed
- [ ] **Tab:** Leave the feed

### Chat message (`<focsd-chat-message>`)

Pattern: Article in a feed.

- [ ] An `article` named "You, 9:05 AM" or "Assistant, 9:05 AM" (author and time). The parts render in order: text, reasoning, tool calls, sources and files.
- [ ] User text is shown as plain text; assistant text is markdown (see streaming text).
- [ ] A failed reply shows its error in the message. A stopped one notes "Response stopped". An assistant reply that is done shows its message actions.
- [ ] Retry and feedback from the actions are passed on as `focsd-retry` and `focsd-feedback`.

### Streaming text (`<focsd-streaming-text>`)

Pattern: Static text that grows while it streams.

- [ ] The text is built with DOM calls only (never `innerHTML`), so it runs under a strict Content Security Policy with Trusted Types. Raw HTML, images and tables are shown as text.
- [ ] Links keep `https:`, `http:`, `mailto:` and relative URLs only (`javascript:`, `data:` and the rest become text) and get `rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow"`.
- [ ] Only the last block is rebuilt on each update, so a selection or focus inside finished blocks survives while text streams.
- [ ] The caret is hidden from assistive technology and stops pulsing under reduced motion. Each code block shows its language and has its own copy button. A code block that scrolls sideways is a named region in the tab order, so it scrolls by keyboard; one that fits adds no tab stop.
- [ ] Headings inside a reply are rendered from level 3 down, never as `h1` or `h2`, so they sit under the page’s own headings.
- [ ] On the server the text renders as plain text with its line breaks, so there is content before the script loads.

### Tool call (`<focsd-tool-call>`)

Pattern: Disclosure.

- [ ] A disclosure button named "search_docs, done": the status is a word as well as an icon (running, done or failed), never color alone.
- [ ] Input and output are shown in `pre` blocks as text (`JSON.stringify`, never HTML), so they cannot inject markup. A block that scrolls is a region named "Input" or "Output" in the tab order; one that fits adds no tab stop.
- [ ] It fires the `toggle` event when it opens or closes, like `<details>`, and does not bubble.
- [ ] The running ring does not spin under reduced motion.
- [ ] **Enter / Space:** Open or close the input and output

### Reasoning (`<focsd-reasoning>`)

Pattern: Disclosure.

- [ ] A disclosure button named "Reasoning", or "Reasoning…" while it streams. It is collapsed by default.
- [ ] Its text is plain text and is never announced as it arrives.
- [ ] It fires the `toggle` event when it opens or closes, like `<details>`, and does not bubble.
- [ ] **Enter / Space:** Open or close the reasoning

### Prompt suggestions (`<focsd-prompt-suggestions>`)

Pattern: List of buttons.

- [ ] A list named by `label` (default "Suggestions") of real buttons. Each button is its own tab stop; arrow keys are not used.
- [ ] Choosing one fires `focsd-suggestion-select` with `detail.text`; sending it is up to your app (`chat.send(text)`).
- [ ] At most four are shown, and the list wraps on narrow screens. An empty list renders nothing.
- [ ] **Tab:** Move between suggestions
- [ ] **Enter / Space:** Choose the suggestion

### Message actions (`<focsd-message-actions>`)

Pattern: Toolbar.

- [ ] A `role="toolbar"` named "Message actions" with one tab stop; the arrow keys, Home and End move between the actions (mirrored in right-to-left text).
- [ ] Copy is `focsd-copy-button` and says "Copied". Retry fires `focsd-retry` with the message id.
- [ ] The thumbs are toggle buttons with `aria-pressed`; choosing one announces "Marked as a good response" or "Marked as a bad response", and taking it back announces "Feedback removed". It fires `focsd-feedback` with `value` of `up`, `down` or null.
- [ ] **Arrow Left / Right:** Move between the actions
- [ ] **Home / End:** First / last action
- [ ] **Enter / Space:** Use the action

### Composer (`<focsd-composer>`)

Pattern: Textbox (multi-line) + file drop.

- [ ] A native `<textarea>` named by `label` (default "Message"). It grows to eight lines. Enter sends; Shift+Enter adds a line. Nothing is sent while an input method (IME) composes, so choosing a candidate with Enter never sends.
- [ ] While `busy`, the send button becomes Stop in the same place and keeps focus, so Tab from the field reaches it. It fires `focsd-stop`. Enter does nothing while busy.
- [ ] Send, stop, attach and remove are at least 44 by 44 px. Send is `aria-disabled` rather than `disabled` when there is nothing to send, so it keeps focus.
- [ ] Files can be attached with the button, pasted or dropped on the composer (an outline and "Drop files to attach" show while dragging). A rejected file (type, size or count) is announced assertively with the reason and also shown as text next to the field.
- [ ] `focsd-submit` is cancelable: cancel it to keep the text and files. It sends the text as typed, with `files` as `File` objects.
- [ ] **Enter:** Send (not while composing text with an input method)
- [ ] **Shift + Enter:** New line
- [ ] **Tab:** Move to send or stop

### Attachment tile (`<focsd-attachment-tile>`)

Pattern: List item with a remove button.

- [ ] A list item (`role="listitem"`) with the file name, its size (for example "200 KB") and an icon for its type that is hidden from assistive technology. Place tiles in a `role="list"`.
- [ ] The remove button is named "Remove report.pdf" and is at least 44 by 44 px; it fires `focsd-attachment-remove` with `detail.name`. The tile does not remove itself.
- [ ] `status` is `ready`, `uploading` or `error`; uploading and failed uploads say so in words, not by color alone.
- [ ] **Enter / Space (remove button):** Fire `focsd-attachment-remove`

### Source chip (`<focsd-source-chip>`)

Pattern: Link.

- [ ] A real link named "[1] Feed pattern", underlined, with the host name in muted text.
- [ ] Only `https:`, `http:`, `mailto:` and relative URLs become links. Any other scheme (`javascript:`, `data:`) is shown as text, not a link. Links get `rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow"` and never set `target`.
- [ ] **Enter:** Follow the link

### File changes (`<focsd-file-changes>`)

Pattern: List of buttons (arrow keys).

- [ ] Each file is a button named in full ("src/lib/runs.ts, modified, 24 lines added, 9 removed"); the status letter, colors, counts and bar are hidden from assistive technology, so nothing depends on color.
- [ ] The chosen file has `aria-current="true"`. One file is in the tab order (the chosen one, or the first); arrow keys move between files.
- [ ] Long paths are cut at the start, so the file name stays visible; the full path is in the name.
- [ ] Choosing a file fires `focsd-file-select` with `detail: { path, file }`.
- [ ] **Up / Down:** Previous / next file
- [ ] **Home / End:** First / last file
- [ ] **Enter / Space:** Choose the file
